lead.headline: Listening Act licences required from today; inspection begins tomorrow
lead.deck: 2,842 licences granted in Queens; about 3,150 systems unlicensed, many with owners unknown; eight inspectors to begin in Elmhurst and Astoria at 9 a.m. tomorrow
lead.body: Licences under the Listening Act are required from today for every building listening system in the State. In Queens, Mr. Hollis Crane's office granted 2,842 by its close at 6 p.m. yesterday, the last to a Flushing church which had applied in April. About 3,150 systems in the borough remain unlicensed, his office estimates, the greater part in buildings whose owners cannot be found. Inspection begins at 9 a.m. tomorrow in Elmhurst and Astoria with eight inspectors. Unlicensed systems may be disconnected under section 9.

columns.headline: Athletics lead by nine games; no game at Philadelphia on Sunday
columns.body: The Athletics beat the Yankees at Philadelphia on Friday and lost to them on Saturday, and lead the American League by nine games. No game was played there yesterday, Sunday baseball being prohibited in Pennsylvania. Mr. Babe Ruth's home runs stand at eighteen. Brooklyn divided two with Boston.

columns.headline: Arcade tenants to deposit the July rent with the court clerk at 10 a.m.
columns.body: Mr. Nathan Ewald states that the ten tenants of the Vantry Arcade will deposit the July rent of 412 dollars with Mr. Walter Ingersoll, clerk of the Municipal Court at Long Island City, at 10 a.m. today. The June rent remains with the clerk, uncalled for.

columns.headline: Light company's July bills, with 'Commission credit,' to go out Wednesday
columns.body: Queens Light & Power states that its July bills for about 21,000 subscribers in Astoria and Steinway will be delivered from Wednesday, each showing a 'Commission credit' averaging 19 cents for the half cent collected since May 1. Alderman John Feeney has written again asking that it read 'Refund.'

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states, its shore stations sitting at Rockaway Beach.

speaker.ear: Fair. High 84. Monday. Your walls need papers now. So do you.

lead.headline: Three thousand Queens walls go unlisted, and Crane's inspectors come to call
lead.deck: Licences required from midnight; eight inspectors into Elmhurst and Astoria tomorrow; most of the unlicensed walls belong to landlords nobody can find, which is what makes them landlords
lead.body: From midnight last night every listening wall in the State needs Mr. Crane's licence, and about three thousand in Queens do not have one. Most of them belong to landlords who cannot be found, which in Queens is not unusual. Tomorrow at nine Mr. Crane sends eight inspectors into Elmhurst and Astoria with notebooks and a ruling: an unlicensed wall may be disconnected. Nobody has said how you disconnect a wall. The inspectors have been issued screwdrivers and one ladder between them.

columns.headline: Pun Derby, week five: the field reopens, and the horse lodges an appeal
columns.body: Week five opens today, one-cent stamp, five dollars and a year's Speaker to Friday's winner. Mr. Kehoe's horse, second three weeks running, has lodged an appeal through counsel. The appeal reads 'Neigh.' The judges have asked counsel what it means. Counsel has asked the horse.

columns.headline: The Arcade pays July to the clerk, and the landlord's line stays engaged
columns.body: At ten this morning the Arcade's ten tenants walk the July rent, four hundred and twelve dollars, up to the court clerk in Long Island City, where June's is still sitting. Signal Ground Rents has not called for either. The Arcade pool has the grey coat at evens.

columns.headline: Ask the Operator: 'Will the inspector want to hear my walls?'
columns.body: Madam, he will want to see a licence, and if you have none he will want to see your landlord. If you cannot produce your landlord, you are in good company: neither can most of Elmhurst. Do not give the inspector your opinion of the landlord. The walls already have it.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Mr. Crane's first act of July: a notice on his door reading 'Licences continue to be granted.' His second: lunch.

lead.headline: Arcade tenants deposit the July rent; court clerk now holds 824 dollars
lead.deck: 412 dollars paid in at 10:04 a.m.; the June rent, read and left on Friday by a man in a grey coat, still uncalled for; Mr. Raab finds the company's post box 'not rented' a seventh time
lead.body: The ten tenants of the Vantry Arcade deposited the July rent of 412 dollars with Mr. Walter Ingersoll, clerk of the Municipal Court at Long Island City, at 10:04 a.m. yesterday, Mr. Nathan Ewald states. The clerk now holds 824 dollars to the credit of Signal Ground Rents Inc., the June rent having been read and left on Friday by a man in a grey coat. Mr. Raab, process server, tried the company's post box a seventh time at 2 p.m. and found it 'not rented.'

columns.headline: Jamaica Signal Exchange permits three households to remain disconnected
columns.body: The Jamaica Signal Exchange states that the three Jamaica households which asked on June 26 to remain disconnected may do so 'on written application, without charge, for the present.' The Exchange has received five further applications since Friday, all from Jamaica.

columns.headline: Stocks rise on 3,280,000 shares; the ticker's tone entered as 'firm and even'
columns.body: Prices on the Stock Exchange rose yesterday on a volume of 3,280,000 shares, the industrial average closing at 335.4, a gain of 1.6. The ticker ran 2 minutes late at the close. Its tone, as entered in the Exchange's tone book at 3 p.m., was 'firm and even.'

columns.headline: Dr. Strand sails tomorrow at noon on the Cedric from Pier 60
columns.body: Dr. Matthias Strand of Union Seminary will sail for Liverpool on the Cedric at noon tomorrow from Pier 60, the seminary states. He travels alone. The chapel's house system was dismantled for repair yesterday, the chapel being closed for July.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states.

speaker.ear: Warmer. High 87. Tuesday. The inspectors are out. Speak well of your walls.

lead.headline: Crane's inspectors make their first calls, and half of Elmhurst won't pick up
lead.deck: Sixty silent walls found by noon, forty doors unanswered; Mr. Pruett waves his licence from the step; one Astoria wall disconnected, and goes on as before
lead.body: Mr. Crane's eight inspectors went into Elmhurst and Astoria at nine this morning to find unlicensed walls, and by noon had found sixty, mostly by standing in hallways and coughing. Nobody came to the door at forty of them. On Whitney Avenue Mr. Pruett showed his licence before he was asked and offered the inspector coffee, which was refused under the regulations. On Ditmars Avenue an inspector disconnected his first wall with a screwdriver, and the wall went on as before. He has filed a report.

columns.headline: The ticker gets a tone of its own, and Wall Street sounds firm on the line
columns.body: The Stock Exchange now writes down how the ticker sounds as well as what it says, and the Record prints both. Yesterday it was 'firm and even.' The industrials rose a point and a half. Our financial editor, who is also our racing editor, calls the ticker 'chirpy.'

columns.headline: Jamaica's quiet set grows to eight, and the Exchange leaves them off the line
columns.body: The three Jamaica households who asked to stay disconnected after the storm may do so, free, for the present, the Signal Exchange says. Five more have asked since Friday. Our man asked one why. She said the house was nicer without an audience.

columns.headline: Strand sails tomorrow, and the chapel's machine goes out of service
columns.body: Dr. Strand boards the Cedric at noon tomorrow for Wales, alone, and the seminary has taken the chapel's machine to pieces for July. The seminary says the two things are unconnected. So, now, is the chapel.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Mr. Raab's seventh visit to the company's post box: 'not rented.' He says the box is starting to recognise him.

lead.headline: Inspectors find 112 unlicensed systems in Elmhurst and Astoria on the first day
lead.deck: 304 buildings visited; 71 doors unanswered; three systems disconnected under section 9; one at Ditmars Avenue continues to record after disconnection, the inspector states
lead.body: Eight inspectors of Mr. Hollis Crane's office visited 304 buildings in Elmhurst and Astoria yesterday and found 112 listening systems without a licence, his office states. No person answered at 71 of them. Three systems were disconnected under section 9, the others being given ten days. A system disconnected at Ditmars Avenue, Astoria, at 11:20 a.m. continued to record, the inspector, Mr. Elwood Baines, states, and has been referred to the Queens Signal Exchange.

columns.headline: Senate vault's record of March 27 unclaimed in its fifteenth week
columns.body: Mr. Lyman Pratt, Clerk of the Senate, states that the committee room's record of March 27 containing the word 'resent' remains unclaimed in the vault at Albany in its fifteenth week. Senator Rufus Keel has written a fifth time. The Senate does not sit until January.

columns.headline: Navy begins clearing the Lakehurst hangar for the Graf Zeppelin in August
columns.body: The Navy began yesterday to clear the great hangar at Lakehurst for the Graf Zeppelin's arrival in August, the Naval Air Station states. A ground crew of 350 sailors will be drilled weekly. A receiving station is to be installed at the mast to hear the ship from 300 miles.

columns.headline: Light company's July bills delivered from today; 'Commission credit' unaltered
columns.body: Queens Light & Power begins delivering its July bills in Astoria and Steinway today, each bearing a line reading 'Commission credit,' the company states. The company has declined Alderman John Feeney's request that the line read 'Refund,' a credit 'not being a refund.'

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states.

speaker.ear: Hot. High 90. Wednesday. Strand sails at noon. Tomorrow, bangs.

lead.headline: Strand sails at noon, and leaves the whole seminary on hold till September
lead.deck: The Cedric backs out of Pier 60 on time; the Doctor cups his ear at our question and goes below; the chapel's machine in a crate till he comes home
lead.body: At noon today the Cedric backed out of Pier 60 with Dr. Strand aboard, bound for Liverpool and then Wales, and nobody at the rail knew why. He waved to no one in particular. Our man shouted from the pier, 'Is it about the word?' and Dr. Strand cupped his ear, smiled and went below. The seminary says the visit is private. The chapel is shut for July and its machine is in a crate. He is back in September, with or without an answer.

columns.headline: Astoria wall is disconnected, keeps taking notes, and the inspector takes leave
columns.body: Inspector Baines unscrewed an unlicensed machine on Ditmars Avenue yesterday at twenty past eleven and listened to it go on recording. He screwed it back, unscrewed it again and listened again. He has referred it to the Signal Exchange, and himself to his doctor.

columns.headline: Light bills bring nineteen cents of credit, and Feeney's refund won't connect
columns.body: The July light bills came to Astoria this morning with nineteen cents of 'Commission credit' on them, and the company has told Alderman Feeney it will not call it a refund. A Steinway widow whose credit came to half a cent has had it framed.

columns.headline: Where's WORS? Ten nights of dead air, and Pike's men are getting a tan
columns.body: Ten nights since WORS read its figures at Rockaway, and Mr. Pike's shore men sit on the sand till midnight with nothing on sixteen-ten. They are now as brown as saddles. Our office boy's pin ninety-eight is still in the sand at Beach 98th Street, slightly rusted.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Dr. Strand's first wireless from the Cedric, to the seminary: 'Calm.' The seminary says that is all of it.

record.ear: Hot. High 91. Low 74. Fair for the fireworks, the Bureau states.

lead.headline: Independence Day fireworks to be recorded in every borough tonight and compared
lead.deck: 212 public buildings to record from 8 p.m. to midnight, as on Armistice Day; 17 licensed displays in the city, five in Queens; private discharge unlawful
lead.body: The Mayor's office states that the house systems of 212 public buildings will record the city's Independence Day fireworks from 8 p.m. to midnight tonight, 'so that the boroughs may be compared,' as was done with the Armistice silence. Queens will be represented by Borough Hall, the Long Island City courthouse and the Jamaica pumping station. Fireworks may lawfully be discharged only at the 17 public displays licensed by the Fire Department, five of them in Queens. Hospitals are asked to keep their dressing rooms staffed.

columns.headline: Stocks close higher before the holiday; ticker's tone 'brisk, slightly sharp'
columns.body: Prices rose for the third day yesterday on a volume of 3,740,000 shares, the industrial average closing at 339.1. The ticker ran 4 minutes late at the close. The tone book records its tone at 3 p.m. as 'brisk, slightly sharp.' The Exchange is closed today.

columns.headline: Dr. Strand sails on the Cedric; one wireless message received
columns.body: Dr. Matthias Strand sailed for Liverpool on the Cedric at noon yesterday, the seminary states. A wireless message received from the ship at 6:12 p.m. read 'Calm.' The seminary states that it was addressed to the chapel, which is closed.

columns.headline: Ice companies deliver 4,100 tons in Queens in a day, the season's most
columns.body: The Astoria Lake, Jamaica Pond and Flushing Bay ice companies delivered 4,100 tons in Queens yesterday, the most in a day this season, Mr. Gustave Pohl states, with 34 wagons. Ice remains at 55 cents the hundredweight. The companies will deliver this morning until noon.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states.

speaker.ear: Hot. High 91. Thursday. The Fourth. Keep your fingers. Count them tonight.

lead.headline: Queens puts the Fourth on the record tonight, and every wall waits for the bang
lead.deck: Two hundred and twelve public walls set to listen from eight till midnight; at Armistice the city compared its silences, tonight it compares its noise
lead.body: Tonight from eight till midnight two hundred and twelve public buildings will take down the city's fireworks so the Mayor can compare the boroughs, as he did with the Armistice silence. That was a contest in keeping quiet. Tonight Queens intends to win the other way. Five licensed displays are promised in the borough, and every boy in Corona has a cellar full of unlicensed ones. The hospitals are ready. Keep the dog in. Keep the boy in, if you can catch him.

columns.headline: Ask the Operator: 'Can I ring the fireworks to start?'
columns.body: Sir, the fireworks are not on the exchange. The operator works tonight from six until two and expects four thousand calls about noise, two hundred about dogs and one about the Hum, which will not be heard tonight, by anybody.

columns.headline: Ice men work the holiday, and Duchess draws the line at noon
columns.body: Four thousand tons of ice went out yesterday, the season's record, on thirty-four wagons. The ice men work till noon today. Duchess will do the Steinway route in a red, white and blue hat, and has made it clear she is going home at twelve sharp.

columns.headline: The ticker sounds sharp, and Wall Street rings up a third day
columns.body: The industrials rose again yesterday, the third day running, and the ticker's tone was entered at three o'clock as 'brisk, slightly sharp.' Our financial editor says sharp is good. Our music critic says sharp is wrong. They are not speaking.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Corona at nine: the first rocket, unlicensed, from a roof on 104th Street. A cheer, a dog, a second rocket.

lead.headline: Fireworks recorded in 212 buildings; Queens loudest of the five boroughs
lead.deck: Queens loudest from 9:10 p.m. to 10:40 p.m. on a first hearing; Exchange logs 4,306 calls; 43 treated for burns; 180 pounds of unlicensed fireworks seized in Corona
lead.body: The house systems of 212 public buildings recorded the city's fireworks from 8 p.m. to midnight last night, and Queens was the loudest of the five boroughs from 9:10 p.m. to 10:40 p.m., the Mayor's office states on a first hearing. The Borough Hall system recorded 1,940 reports between 9 p.m. and 10 p.m. The Queens Exchange logged 4,306 calls, about half concerning noise. Forty-three persons were treated for burns in Queens, two seriously. The police seized 180 pounds of unlicensed fireworks in Corona.

columns.headline: Mr. Ruth hits his nineteenth home run; Yankees divide a holiday double-header
columns.body: Mr. Babe Ruth hit his nineteenth home run of the season in the first game of a double-header at the Stadium yesterday, the Yankees dividing the two before about 45,000. The Athletics won twice and lead the American League by ten games. Brooklyn lost twice.

columns.headline: Inspectors find 61 more unlicensed systems; Ditmars Avenue cut at the street
columns.body: Mr. Hollis Crane's inspectors found 61 further unlicensed systems in Elmhurst and Astoria on Wednesday, 173 in all, his office states. The system at Ditmars Avenue, Astoria, which continued to record after disconnection on Tuesday, was disconnected at the street by the Signal Exchange at 4 p.m.

columns.headline: Phonautograph Society to meet Monday on whether to keep the tone on its records
columns.body: The Phonautograph Society of Queens will hold a special meeting at 8 p.m. on Monday at its rooms in Elmhurst to decide whether the 41-cycle tone on its Alley Pond records 'shall be kept for 1978 or removed,' the secretary, Mr. Linus Fahey, states. Mr. Cyril Abbot will move that it be kept.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states. Its shore stations at Rockaway logged fireworks only.

speaker.ear: Hot. High 92. Friday. Fourteen Fridays. Ears still ringing.

lead.headline: Queens goes off loudest in the city, and the Mayor's walls confirm the report
lead.deck: Nineteen hundred and forty bangs an hour on the Borough Hall machine; Brooklyn beaten by a rocket; forty-three burnt, and Corona's cellars lighter by a hundred and eighty pounds
lead.body: It is official, on a first hearing: Queens was the loudest borough in the city last night from ten past nine until twenty to eleven, beating Brooklyn by a rocket. Borough Hall's walls counted nineteen hundred and forty bangs in an hour. The Exchange took four thousand three hundred calls, half about the noise and half making it. Forty-three were burnt, two badly, and the police carried a hundred and eighty pounds of rockets out of Corona cellars. Corona says that was the spare.

columns.headline: Pun Derby, week five: the operator weds the lineman, and the judges ring off
columns.body: Week five goes to Miss Alma Rourke, switchboard, of Woodside: 'When the operator married the lineman, she got the ring and he got off the hook.' Five dollars and a year's Speaker. Mr. Kehoe's horse placed second again, with 'Hay, operator.' Its appeal is pending.

columns.headline: Party Line's fourteenth Friday, and she won't even come to the window
columns.body: Fourteen Fridays. For the first time Party Line did not come to the parcel window at four. She sat on the warm end of the board, where the Corona calls come in, until six. No tin came anyway. Sergeant Moran says the warrant is current.

columns.headline: Abbot calls the Society to order, and the members tune up for a row
columns.body: Mr. Abbot's Phonautograph Society meets Monday night to decide whether the forty-one cycles stay on the Alley Pond records for 1978. Mr. Abbot says keep them. Half the members say cut them. Puns on the Hum are still disqualified, so we will say no more.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Brooklyn's Mr. Tully says Brooklyn was louder and the Mayor's machines were in the wrong places. He has sent a notice.

lead.headline: Navy to listen for the Graf Zeppelin from seven stations, Lakehurst to Montauk
lead.deck: Ship to be heard 'some hours before she is sighted'; 350 sailors drill at the mast with a weighted line; 17 tank cars of fuel gas ordered for the August visit
lead.body: The Navy will hear the Graf Zeppelin's approach in August from seven receiving stations between Lakehurst and Montauk Point, the Naval Air Station at Lakehurst states, and expects to hear the ship 'some hours before she is sighted.' A ground crew of 350 sailors drilled at the mast for the first time yesterday, catching a weighted line dropped from its head. Seventeen tank cars of fuel gas have been ordered. The Zeppelin company states that the ship will leave Friedrichshafen about August 1.

columns.headline: Week's count: 1,301 night calls on the tone in Queens; 870 on the Brooklyn door
columns.body: The Queens Exchange logged 1,301 calls between 1 a.m. and 4 a.m. in the seven nights to Friday reporting a tone, against 1,262, Superintendent Wilfred Arne states, excluding the night of the Fourth, when such calls 'were not separable.' The Brooklyn Exchange's door shows 870.

columns.headline: No parcel for Position 43 on a fourteenth Friday; the animal stays at the board
columns.body: No parcel addressed to 'Party Line, Queens Exchange, Position 43' was received yesterday, the fourteenth Friday without one, the supervisor states. The animal did not come to the parcel window and remained at the board until 6 p.m. The warrant for Mr. Joseph Marchetti, lineman, remains outstanding.

columns.headline: Licence inspection: 1,020 buildings visited; 296 systems unlicensed; 14 cut
columns.body: Mr. Hollis Crane's inspectors visited 1,020 buildings in Elmhurst and Astoria in the three working days to Friday and found 296 unlicensed systems, 14 being disconnected, his office states. Licences granted in the week numbered 211, 3,053 in all. Inspection moves to Corona and Jackson Heights on Monday.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states.

speaker.ear: Fair. High 89. Saturday. The Mayor counted the bangs. Count your fingers.

lead.headline: Navy will hear the Zeppelin coming, and 350 sailors practise holding the line
lead.deck: Seven listening stations from Lakehurst to Montauk; the ground crew drills with a weighted rope and catches one petty officer; the office boy sends a second sandwich
lead.body: The Navy at Lakehurst means to hear the Graf Zeppelin hours before it sees her, from seven stations strung out to Montauk, and yesterday three hundred and fifty sailors practised catching her. There being no Zeppelin, they caught a weighted rope dropped from the mast, a hundred times, and once a petty officer. The Navy is satisfied. The ship leaves Germany about the first of August. Our office boy's application for a berth is in its second week. He has sent a second sandwich.

columns.headline: Week's count: the tone calls climb, and the Fourth drowns out a night
columns.body: Queens rang about the night tone thirteen hundred and one times this week, up again, the Fourth not counted because nobody could hear anything over Corona. Brooklyn's door reads eight hundred and seventy. Mr. Tully says Brooklyn's fireworks were louder anyway.

columns.headline: Crane's men find 300 walls without papers, and Corona gets the call next
columns.body: Mr. Crane's inspectors have found two hundred and ninety-six unlicensed walls in three days and silenced fourteen. On Monday they go to Corona, which has heard they are coming and has begun licensing in a hurry. Some of Corona has begun moving walls.

columns.headline: The Listening Lady: a proposal between rockets, and it had to be repeated
columns.body: Darlings, the Listening Lady spent the Fourth on a Jackson Heights roof, where Mr. Sol Greaves proposed to Miss Ada Fenn between rockets and had to say it three times. She said yes after the second rocket and again after the third, for safety.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Mr. Pike's men are packing up at Rockaway. Long Beach is ringing the Exchange. We are sending a man with a bicycle.

editorial.headline: Independence is for nations, not stenographers
editorial.body: On the Fourth of July the Speaker reminds its readers what independence means: it is the freedom of a nation from a foreign king, not the freedom of a stenographer from her employer. Miss Penrose, who has typed this column every week for nine years, has asked this week for a Saturday off, a raise, and the right to sign her own name to the letters she composes in mine. This is the influence of Lilith on the women of our own offices. We have refused all three. Miss Penrose has accepted our refusal with a smile we did not care for, and has typed this editorial, we notice, without a single error. That has never happened before.

columns.headline: Fourth's fingers counted: the borough is nine short, and Corona wants a recount
columns.body: The Board of Health finished its count of Thursday's rockets and reports twenty-two burned hands in Queens, one lost eyebrow and a goat in Ozone Park that has not come home. The Mayor counted the bangs. Corona has requested a recount of the goat.

columns.headline: The Pun Derby: this week's winner goes off with a bang, regrettably
columns.body: This week's five dollars goes to a Ridgewood man who says the Fourth was a blast for all concerned and that his brother-in-law made a real Roman candle of himself. The brother-in-law is well. The judges remain on the fence. One-cent stamp.

columns.headline: Ask the Operator: 'Can you tell me whose dog that is?'
columns.body: Sir, the dog has been on your party line since Tuesday and is on good terms with the whole of Sunnyside. The operator knows whose it is and has been asked not to say. Try a bone, and do not put it on the wire.

columns.headline: Miss Wills keeps the title; our smile inquiry gets no return
columns.body: Miss Helen Wills beat Miss Helen Jacobs six-one, six-two and retained her Wimbledon title, the wire states. Our sporting editor asks whether a lady champion ought to look pleased. We have put the question to London and are keeping the line open for a suitable reply.

back.foot: The Speaker. Our corrections are funnier than their news.

lead.headline: WORS 1610 heard at Long Beach at 11:02 p.m.; stations at Rockaway hear nothing
lead.deck: Nine minutes of figures heard from the direction of a closed bandstand with no system; the Rockaway stations, five miles west, log nothing; the Division to 'move east'
lead.body: WORS 1610 was heard at Long Beach, Nassau County, at 11:02 p.m. yesterday, its first transmission since June 22, the Radio Division states. About 150 persons on the boardwalk near National Boulevard heard about nine minutes of figures from the direction of the bandstand, which was closed. The Long Beach police state that the bandstand has no system. Mr. Harold Pike's shore stations at Rockaway Beach, about five miles west, heard nothing on 1610. Mr. Pike states that the Division will 'move east.'

columns.headline: Exchange logs 207 inquiries on WORS 1610, 61 of them from the Rockaways
columns.body: The Queens Exchange logged 207 inquiries concerning WORS 1610 between 11:10 p.m. and 1 a.m., Superintendent Wilfred Arne states, 61 of them from the Rockaways, whose callers stated that they had heard nothing. The Long Beach exchange logged 'about 90.'

columns.headline: Phonautograph Society meets tomorrow on the tone; Mrs. Grieve admitted as guest
columns.body: The Phonautograph Society of Queens will meet at 8 p.m. tomorrow at its rooms in Elmhurst on the motion of Mr. Cyril Abbot that the tone be kept on the Alley Pond records 'as heard.' Mrs. Ottoline Grieve, who is not a member, has been admitted as a guest at the request of 12 members.

columns.headline: Atlas Casualty Co. to hear Mrs. Dorr's claim at 2 p.m. on Tuesday
columns.body: The Atlas Casualty Co. states that it will hear the claim of Mrs. Agnes Dorr for the kitchen fire of March 9 at Whitney Avenue, Elmhurst, at 2 p.m. on Tuesday at its offices in Jamaica. Mrs. Dorr has asked that the company's house system be switched off for the hearing.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: Mr. Pike's shore stations will sit at Long Beach from 10:30 p.m. tonight, the Radio Division states.

speaker.ear: Hot. High 90. Sunday. WORS moved house. No forwarding address.

lead.headline: WORS moves to Long Beach, and Pike's men are sitting at the wrong exchange
lead.deck: Nine minutes of figures on the Long Beach boardwalk from a bandstand with no machine in it; Rockaway, sitting up for it, hears the tide; Mr. Pike packs his deck chairs
lead.body: Mr. Pike's men sat at Rockaway for two weeks waiting for WORS, and last night at two minutes past eleven it turned up five miles east at Long Beach, reading figures to a hundred and fifty people on the boardwalk from the direction of a bandstand with no machine in it. Rockaway heard nothing. Rockaway is furious. Mr. Pike says he will move east. Our man on the bicycle arrived at twenty past, in time to hear the boardwalk arguing about whether it had heard anything at all.

columns.headline: Where's WORS? Pin ninety-nine leaves Queens, and the map needs an extension
columns.body: Pin ninety-nine has gone in at Long Beach, which is off the edge of our map of Queens, so the office boy has pasted on a piece of Nassau cut from a railroad timetable. He says WORS is heading east. He is twelve, but nobody has a better idea.

columns.headline: Ask the Operator: 'Is Long Beach in Queens?'
columns.body: Madam, no, it is in Nassau, and the operator cannot put you through without a toll. WORS appears not to pay tolls. The Rockaway callers who rang last night to report hearing nothing have been charged for the call, which some think unjust.

columns.headline: Mrs. Grieve gets a seat at the Society, and the meeting finds its frequency
columns.body: Twelve of Mr. Abbot's members asked that Mrs. Grieve be let in tomorrow night as a guest, and she has been. She will sit at the back. Mr. Abbot will sit at the front. The motion is whether to keep the forty-one cycles. Tickets are not available.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Long Beach at eleven tonight: Mr. Pike's men, three hundred on the boardwalk, our man on the bicycle. Not a figure.

record.ear: Hot. High 94. Low 76. No relief before Thursday, the Bureau states.

lead.headline: Temperature 95 at 3:10 p.m., the year's highest; 20 playgrounds open tonight
lead.deck: Bureau sees no relief before Thursday; 520,000 at Rockaway; three overcome in Queens; roof sleepers asked to keep a parapet between themselves and the street
lead.body: The temperature reached 95 degrees at 3:10 p.m. yesterday, the highest of the year, the Weather Bureau states, and the Bureau forecasts no relief before Thursday. About 520,000 persons visited Rockaway Beach. Three persons were overcome in Queens. The Board of Health will open 20 school playgrounds as sleeping grounds from 9 p.m. tonight, and asks that persons sleeping on roofs keep a parapet between themselves and the street. The Queens Exchange logged 1,880 calls between 10 p.m. and 2 a.m.

columns.headline: Mr. Ruth hits his twentieth home run; the Athletics lead by eleven games
columns.body: Mr. Babe Ruth hit his twentieth home run of the season at the Stadium yesterday, the Yankees winning before about 50,000. The Athletics won on Saturday and lead the American League by eleven games. Brooklyn lost twice at Ebbets Field.

columns.headline: Radio Division's stations at Long Beach hear nothing on Sunday night
columns.body: Mr. Harold Pike's shore stations sat at Long Beach from 10:30 p.m. to midnight yesterday and heard nothing on 1610, the Radio Division states. About 300 persons attended on the boardwalk. Rockaway Beach was not watched, for the first night since June 23.

columns.headline: Licence inspectors move to Corona and Jackson Heights; 23 records still held
columns.body: Mr. Hollis Crane's inspectors begin in Corona and Jackson Heights at 9 a.m. today, his office states. The office granted 62 licences on Saturday, chiefly to Corona applicants. The records of the 23 disputed primary districts remain in its vault 'pending an application by the Board of Elections.'

record.wire: LATE WIRE: The Phonautograph Society meets at 8 p.m. tonight at Elmhurst. The doors will be closed at 8:05 p.m., the secretary states.

speaker.ear: Hot. High 94. Monday. Ninety-five yesterday. Sleep upstairs.

lead.headline: Ninety-five in the shade, and Queens goes to sleep out of range
lead.deck: The year's worst heat, and a walk-up's machine stops at the ceiling; whole families say what they like on the tar; the Board of Health asks for a parapet
lead.body: It was ninety-five yesterday afternoon, the year's worst, and last night Queens went back up to the roofs and fire escapes, and this time it went for privacy too. A walk-up's machine stops at the ceiling. So in Sunnyside, Astoria and Ridgewood whole families slept on the tar where nothing took them down, and said what they liked. The Board of Health asks sleepers to keep a parapet between themselves and the street. A Ridgewood man rolled over twice and hit his mother-in-law.

columns.headline: Babe connects for twenty, and Philadelphia keeps the Yanks on hold at eleven
columns.body: The Babe hit his twentieth at the Stadium yesterday before fifty thousand in their shirtsleeves, a long one to right. Philadelphia is eleven clear. Mr. Huggins says July is long. Mr. Huggins says every month is long. It is that kind of season.

columns.headline: Pun Derby, week six: the cards come in by the hundredweight, and half are cold
columns.body: Week six opens with eight hundred postcards in the Monday post, two hundred of them about ice. The early leader is a Woodside grocer: 'My radio man never married. Every girl he took out gave him static, and the last one gave him the air.' Mr. Kehoe's horse has entered again.

columns.headline: Ask the Operator: 'Is the roof on the record?'
columns.body: Sir, not in an ordinary walk-up, where the machine stops at the ceiling. The operator cannot speak for your roof, which may be extraordinary. If in doubt, whisper. If your neighbour on the next roof is listening, that is not a machine. That is Mrs. Halloran, and she is unlicensed.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: The Phonautograph Society's doors shut at five past eight. At twenty to ten they opened again, and fourteen members came out first.

lead.headline: Phonautograph Society divides on the tone; 14 members withdraw
lead.deck: Mr. Abbot's motion carried 19 to 14 at 9:38 p.m.; the 14 to found a Phonautograph Circle of Flushing 'to record what is meant to be heard'; Mrs. Grieve present, silent
lead.body: The Phonautograph Society of Queens voted 19 to 14 at Elmhurst last night that the tone of 41 cycles be kept on its Alley Pond records 'as heard,' on the motion of Mr. Cyril Abbot, the secretary, Mr. Linus Fahey, states. The 14 withdrew at 9:40 p.m. and state that they will form the Phonautograph Circle of Flushing, to record 'what is meant to be heard.' Mrs. Ottoline Grieve, present as a guest, did not speak. The meeting's record is held by the Society.

columns.headline: Second day of heat: 94 at 2:40 p.m.; about 2,400 sleep in the playgrounds
columns.body: The temperature reached 94 degrees at 2:40 p.m. yesterday, the Weather Bureau states. About 2,400 persons slept in the 20 school playgrounds opened by the Board of Health, and four were overcome in Queens. The Bureau forecasts 95 degrees today.

columns.headline: Stocks rise on 4,110,000 shares; the ticker's tone entered as 'hurried, rising'
columns.body: Prices on the Stock Exchange rose yesterday on a volume of 4,110,000 shares, the industrial average closing at 342.6, a gain of 3.5. The ticker ran 7 minutes late at the close. The tone book records its tone at 3 p.m. as 'hurried, rising.'

columns.headline: Atlas hears Mrs. Dorr's claim at 2 p.m. today with its own system off
columns.body: The Atlas Casualty Co. will hear the claim of Mrs. Agnes Dorr at its Jamaica offices at 2 p.m. today, the company states, and has agreed to her request that its house system be switched off for the hearing, 'the company having no need of it.' Notes will be taken by pencil.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states, its shore stations sitting at Long Beach.

speaker.ear: Hot. High 95. Tuesday. A society splits. The birds stay neutral.

lead.headline: Abbot's Society splits down the frequency, and fourteen walk out on a high note
lead.deck: Nineteen to fourteen to keep the forty-one cycles for 1978; the fourteen found a Flushing Circle by eleven; Mrs. Grieve sits silent at the back and leaves by the same door
lead.body: Last night at Elmhurst the Phonautograph Society voted nineteen to fourteen to keep the forty-one cycles on its Alley Pond records for 1978, as heard. At twenty to ten the fourteen stood up and walked out into the heat, and by eleven had founded the Phonautograph Circle of Flushing, to record what is meant to be heard. Who decides what is meant they did not say. Mrs. Grieve sat at the back with her handbag on her knee and said nothing all night. She left by the same door as the fourteen.

columns.headline: Ninety-four, and the schoolyards ring with snoring at full volume
columns.body: Twenty-four hundred people slept in the twenty schoolyards last night, with a patrolman and a tap in each, and snored at a volume the Board of Health had not foreseen. A Corona schoolyard kept its janitor awake till four. He says it was louder than the Fourth.

columns.headline: The ticker runs seven minutes behind, and Wall Street can't get a word in
columns.body: The ticker ran seven minutes late yesterday because the market rose faster than it could say so, and the Exchange's tone book calls it 'hurried, rising.' Our financial editor says a hurried ticker is a happy ticker. Our music critic says it is a soprano.

columns.headline: Mrs. Dorr goes to Atlas today, and asks them to switch off the listening
columns.body: Mrs. Dorr meets the Atlas Casualty Co. in Jamaica at two this afternoon about her kitchen, and the company has agreed to switch its own machine off for it, by request. Notes by pencil. We expect Mrs. Dorr will bring her own pencil.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Atlas, a quarter past four: Mrs. Dorr came out smiling. The company came out with its pencil worn down.

lead.headline: Atlas Casualty Co. allows Mrs. Dorr's claim; 380 dollars for the March 9 fire
lead.deck: Hearing of 112 minutes with the company's system off at the claimant's request; notes by pencil; 'I said it once, and that will do'
lead.body: The Atlas Casualty Co. allowed the claim of Mrs. Agnes Dorr for the kitchen fire of March 9 at Whitney Avenue, Elmhurst, at its Jamaica offices yesterday, and will pay 380 dollars, the company states. The hearing lasted from 2 p.m. to 3:52 p.m., the company's house system being switched off at Mrs. Dorr's request and notes taken by pencil. Mrs. Dorr states that she 'said it once, and that will do.' The company states that no record of the hearing exists.

columns.headline: Third day of heat: 95 at 3:20 p.m.; Board of Health opens 12 more playgrounds
columns.body: The temperature reached 95 degrees at 3:20 p.m. yesterday, equalling Sunday's, the Weather Bureau states. The Board of Health opened 12 more playgrounds, 32 in all, and about 3,900 persons slept in them. Six were overcome in Queens. Thunderstorms are forecast for tomorrow night.

columns.headline: Senate vault's record of March 27 unclaimed in its sixteenth week
columns.body: Mr. Lyman Pratt, Clerk of the Senate, states that the committee room's record of March 27 containing the word 'resent' remains in the vault at Albany, unclaimed, in its sixteenth week. Mr. Pratt states that the vault is kept at 61 degrees.

columns.headline: Phonautograph Circle of Flushing meets; Mr. Irving Moss elected president
columns.body: The 14 members who withdrew from the Phonautograph Society of Queens on Monday met at the Flushing Free Library last night and elected Mr. Irving Moss, pharmacist, president of the Phonautograph Circle of Flushing, the library states. Mrs. Ottoline Grieve declined office. Mr. Cyril Abbot states that 'the Society is entire.'

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states.

speaker.ear: Hot. High 95. Wednesday. Ice is gold. Horses are saints.

lead.headline: Atlas hears Mrs. Dorr off the record, and her claim finally gets through
lead.deck: Machine switched off at her request; an hour and fifty-two minutes in pencil; three hundred and eighty dollars for a kitchen that was heard too often
lead.body: For four months the Atlas Casualty Co. listened to Mrs. Dorr's kitchen and said no. Yesterday it switched its machine off, sharpened a pencil and heard Mrs. Dorr instead, for an hour and fifty-two minutes, and said yes: three hundred and eighty dollars for the fire. Mrs. Dorr told our man she had said it once and that would do. Atlas says no record of the hearing exists, which for once is what everybody wanted. Mr. Harsch, the old adjuster, is still on leave.

columns.headline: Breakaway Circle picks a pharmacist, and Abbot says his line is unbroken
columns.body: The fourteen who walked out on Mr. Abbot met in the Flushing library last night and named themselves the Phonautograph Circle, with Mr. Moss the pharmacist in the chair. Mrs. Grieve was offered office and declined. Mr. Abbot says the Society is entire. It is now nineteen.

columns.headline: The Senate vault holds at sixty-one, and 'resent' keeps cool on the record
columns.body: The Albany vault holding 'resent' is kept at sixty-one degrees, the Senate clerk says, which makes it the coolest word in New York this week. It has been there sixteen weeks. Senator Keel asked whether he might visit it. He may not. He asked about the temperature.

columns.headline: Ask the Operator: 'Where can I get ice?' The line is busy
columns.body: Madam, the operator has been asked this four hundred times today and has no ice either. The wagons are out at dawn and empty by noon. Mr. Pohl says rise early. The operator rises at five and still lost to a Mrs. Blum of Woodside with a pram.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Woodside at noon: the Astoria Lake wagon met by sixty housewives and a priest. The priest got none.

record.ear: Hot. High 96. Low 78. Thunderstorms tonight, the Bureau states.

lead.headline: Ice companies deliver 5,300 tons in Queens, the most in a day since 1925
lead.deck: Every wagon empty by 12:40 p.m.; 600 tons a day sought from the Hudson houses at Rockland Lake; price unchanged at 55 cents the hundredweight
lead.body: The Astoria Lake, Jamaica Pond and Flushing Bay ice companies delivered 5,300 tons in Queens yesterday on 38 wagons, the most in a single day since July 1925, Mr. Gustave Pohl states. Every wagon was empty by 12:40 p.m. The companies have asked for 600 tons a day from the Hudson ice houses at Rockland Lake until the heat breaks. Ice remains at 55 cents the hundredweight. The Board of Health asks that ice for households with infants be delivered first.

columns.headline: Stocks rise again; the ticker 15 minutes late; its tone 'shrill at the close'
columns.body: Prices on the Stock Exchange rose again yesterday on a volume of 4,620,000 shares, the industrial average closing at 347.0, a gain of 2.2. The ticker ran 15 minutes late at the close. The tone book records its tone at 3 p.m. as 'shrill at the close,' the first such entry this year.

columns.headline: Lakehurst receiving station tested; the Los Angeles heard at 260 miles
columns.body: The Navy tested its receiving station at the Lakehurst mast on Tuesday night and heard the airship Los Angeles, on a flight over Cape May, at 260 miles, the Naval Air Station states. The station is to hear the Graf Zeppelin from 300 miles in August.

columns.headline: Court clerk's letter to the company's box 'called for,' the post office states
columns.body: The letter of Mr. Walter Ingersoll, clerk of the Municipal Court, to the post office box of Signal Ground Rents Inc. was called for on Tuesday, the post office states, the box being 'not rented.' The post office does not state by whom. Mr. Raab was at Elmhurst.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states.

speaker.ear: Hot. High 96. Thursday. Thunder tonight. Then the cat can come in.

lead.headline: Five thousand tons of ice by noon, and Queens gives the wagons a warm reception
lead.deck: Thirty-eight wagons empty by twenty to one; prams at the kerb in Woodside, a pail under the drip in Corona; Duchess does the Steinway route twice and is kissed
lead.body: Thirty-eight ice wagons left the houses at dawn yesterday with five thousand three hundred tons, the most since 1925, and by twenty to one every one of them was empty and going home on a dry floor. In Woodside sixty housewives met the Astoria Lake wagon with prams. In Corona a man followed it four blocks with a pail, catching the drip. Duchess did the Steinway route twice and was kissed by a grandmother. Mr. Pohl is sending up the Hudson for more.

columns.headline: The company's box takes a call, and the post office won't say who answered
columns.body: The court clerk's letter to Signal Ground Rents' post box has been called for, the post office says, though the box is not rented and has not been since Mr. Raab began asking. The post office will not say who called. Mr. Raab was in Elmhurst. The pool has shortened the grey coat.

columns.headline: The ticker's tone goes shrill, and Wall Street hits a high note
columns.body: The ticker ran fifteen minutes behind yesterday, and the Exchange's tone book calls it 'shrill at the close,' the first time this year. The industrials gained again. Our financial editor is buying. Our music critic has asked him to stop.

columns.headline: Pun Derby: the radio man's static leads, and the ice puns melt on the desk
columns.body: Week six is the Woodside grocer's to lose: the radio man whose girls all gave him static, and the last one the air. Two hundred ice puns have been disqualified for arriving in poor condition after the heat. Judging tomorrow.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Thunder over Flushing at a quarter to ten, and rain. Queens comes down from the roofs at last, wet and grateful.

lead.headline: Man in a grey coat reads the Arcade's July rent receipt at the clerk's window
lead.deck: At 3:40 p.m., as on June 28; 'Correct'; 824 dollars left at the window; the company's post box still 'not rented'
lead.body: The man in a grey coat who read the Vantry Arcade's June rent receipt on June 28 returned to the window of the clerk of the Municipal Court at Long Island City at 3:40 p.m. yesterday and asked to see the receipt for the July rent, Mr. Walter Ingersoll states. He read it through, said 'Correct,' and left without asking for the 824 dollars now held. The post office states that the clerk's letter to the company's box was called for on Tuesday. Mr. Raab was at Elmhurst.

columns.headline: Storms end four days of heat; temperature falls 22 degrees in an hour
columns.body: Thunderstorms crossed Queens from 9:45 p.m. to 11:10 p.m. last night, and the temperature fell from 92 to 70 degrees in an hour, the Weather Bureau states. The Board of Health closed its 32 playgrounds at midnight. The Jamaica signal feeder was not struck.

columns.headline: The Cedric due at Liverpool tomorrow; Dr. Strand's second wireless received
columns.body: The Cedric is due at Liverpool tomorrow morning, the White Star Line states. A second wireless message from Dr. Matthias Strand was received by Union Seminary yesterday at 4:20 p.m. It read 'Nearly.' The seminary states that the chapel remains closed.

columns.headline: Jamaica Signal Exchange grants 26 applications to remain disconnected
columns.body: The Jamaica Signal Exchange states that it has granted 26 applications from Jamaica households to remain disconnected, the first three having been made after the storm of June 25. Two applications have been received from Hollis and one from St. Albans. The Exchange states that it 'is not encouraging them.'

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states.

speaker.ear: Cooler. High 81. Friday. Fifteen Fridays. The grey coat came back.

lead.headline: Pun Derby, week six: the radio man gets the air, and the judges get the static
lead.deck: Nine thousand cards in six weeks; Mr. Voss of Woodside takes the five dollars; the horse places second for the fifth time, and its counsel resigns
lead.body: Week six goes to Mr. Martin Voss, grocer, of Woodside, whose radio man could not marry because every girl he took out gave him static and the last one gave him the air. Five dollars and a year's Speaker. Runners-up: a Jackson Heights broker's clerk whose tips come in over the wire and whose margin goes out of it, and a Glendale girl who will not marry an operator because he would always be putting her through it. Mr. Kehoe's horse placed second. Its counsel has resigned.

columns.headline: The grey coat rings at twenty to four, and leaves the rent on hold again
columns.body: At twenty to four yesterday, his hour, the man in the grey coat read the Arcade's July receipt at the court clerk's window, said 'Correct' and walked out, leaving eight hundred and twenty-four dollars behind. Mr. Raab was in Elmhurst. The pool has paid out at evens.

columns.headline: Party Line's fifteenth Friday, and she's back on the line at the window
columns.body: Fifteen Fridays. After last week's absence Party Line was back at the parcel window at four today, sitting straight, ears forward, until half past five. No tin came from Corona. Sergeant Moran says the warrant is current. The clerk says she looked as if she had been told something.

columns.headline: Thunder at last, and Queens comes down from the roof with its ears ringing
columns.body: The storm came over at a quarter to ten and the temperature fell twenty-two degrees in an hour. Queens came down off the tar roofs wet through, and the schoolyards were empty by midnight. Jamaica's feeder held, and Jamaica, for once, was sorry.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Dr. Strand's second wireless to the seminary: 'Nearly.' The seminary says that is all of it, again.

lead.headline: WORS 1610 heard at Port Washington at 11:03 p.m.; stations at Long Beach silent
lead.deck: Seven minutes of figures heard 'from the water' at the town dock; the Division's stations at Long Beach, 18 miles south, hear nothing; both shores to be watched
lead.body: WORS 1610 was heard at Port Washington, on Manhasset Bay, at 11:03 p.m. yesterday for about seven minutes, the Radio Division states, the second transmission since June 22 and the second east of the city line. The town dock's watchman and about 20 persons on the dock heard figures 'from the water.' Mr. Harold Pike's shore stations at Long Beach, about 18 miles south, heard nothing on 1610. Mr. Pike states that the Division will sit on the north shore 'as well.'

columns.headline: Week's count: 1,344 night calls on the tone in Queens; 912 on the Brooklyn door
columns.body: The Queens Exchange logged 1,344 calls between 1 a.m. and 4 a.m. in the seven nights to Friday reporting a tone, against 1,301, Superintendent Wilfred Arne states, the greater part from persons sleeping on roofs. The Brooklyn Exchange's door shows 912.

columns.headline: Dr. Rastin to measure the tone on Jamaica Bay tonight from 9 p.m.
columns.body: Dr. Emil Rastin will measure the tone from a rowboat on Jamaica Bay tonight at nine stations from Broad Channel toward Barren Island, beginning at 9 p.m., his office states. Mr. Pat Mulry of College Point will row. Queens Light & Power states that Jamaica Bay 'is not on its system.'

columns.headline: Licence inspection: 2,410 buildings visited; 512 unlicensed; 39 disconnected
columns.body: Mr. Hollis Crane's inspectors have visited 2,410 buildings in Elmhurst, Astoria, Corona and Jackson Heights and found 512 unlicensed systems, 39 having been disconnected, his office states. Licences granted in the week numbered 268, 3,321 in all. The Board of Elections has not applied.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: The Cedric arrived at Liverpool at 7:10 a.m., the White Star Line states. Dr. Strand took the train for Chester.

speaker.ear: Fair. High 80. Saturday. Rastin rows tonight. Mulry's arms are insured.

lead.headline: WORS rings in from Port Washington, and Pike is caught on the other line
lead.deck: Seven minutes of figures off Manhasset Bay to a watchman and twenty people in the breeze; Long Beach gets the surf; Mr. Pike will now watch both shores
lead.body: Mr. Pike moved his men east to Long Beach to catch WORS, and last night at three minutes past eleven WORS turned up eighteen miles north at Port Washington, reading figures off the water to the night watchman on the town dock and twenty people who had come down for the breeze. Seven minutes, then nothing. Long Beach heard the surf. Mr. Pike says he will now watch both shores, which is most of Long Island. The office boy has run out of timetable.

columns.headline: Where's WORS? Pin one hundred on the north shore, and the map hits the stairs
columns.body: Pin one hundred is in at Port Washington, on a railroad timetable pasted to a Nassau timetable pasted to Queens. The map now reaches the stair rail. The office boy says WORS is going round Long Island. We asked him which way. He says the long way.

columns.headline: Rastin rows Jamaica Bay tonight, and Mulry signs on for a longer line
columns.body: Dr. Rastin goes out from Broad Channel at nine tonight to take the tone at nine stations toward Barren Island, Mr. Mulry rowing. The light company says Jamaica Bay is off its system. Mr. Mulry says it is off his, too, and has asked for two dollars.

columns.headline: The Listening Lady: Strand lands, and Chester takes the call
columns.body: Darlings, the Cedric came into Liverpool this morning and Dr. Strand went straight to the train for Chester and Wales, with one bag and no word for anybody. The Listening Lady's cousin in Chester saw him buy a newspaper and a bun. The bun was currant.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Broad Channel, nine o'clock: Dr. Rastin, Mr. Mulry, one rowboat, one meter, four gulls, and our man in a second boat, bailing.

editorial.headline: Ice trust melts in its own warehouse
editorial.body: In the worst heat of the summer, with ice at sixty cents the hundredweight and the babies of Astoria dying of the milk, the tenements of Ditmars Avenue woke on Friday to find the ice wagons of the Knickerbocker Ice Trust parked at every door and unloading free, the drivers wearing black silk armbands and grinning. The Trust's president, Mr. Lyman Fisk, had, it seems, sold every block in the warehouse to a lady at a dinner party for one cent, in writing, in the course of explaining how he keeps the price so high. The Speaker defends free enterprise. This was certainly enterprise. Mr. Fisk says it was not free. The babies are cooler.

lead.headline: Boy of five lost at Rockaway found through the beach recorder at Beach 116th
lead.deck: Recorder at the lifeguard stand took down his name, his street and 'my mother has a green hat' at 3:31 p.m.; found at 4:05 p.m.; 31 children lost, all found
lead.body: Thomas Gilroy, aged five, of Woodhaven, separated from his mother near Beach 98th Street at 2:15 p.m. yesterday, was found at 4:05 p.m. at Beach 116th Street, the police state. The Parks Department's beach recorder at the lifeguard stand there had taken down his voice at 3:31 p.m. giving his name, his street and 'my mother has a green hat.' The recorders, placed at 12 stands in June, are played in the lost-children tent hourly. Thirty-one children were reported lost yesterday. All were found.

columns.headline: Dr. Rastin's party returns from Jamaica Bay at 1:40 a.m.; figures tomorrow
columns.body: Dr. Emil Rastin and Mr. Pat Mulry returned to Broad Channel at 1:40 a.m. today after taking readings at nine stations on Jamaica Bay, Dr. Rastin's office states. The figures will be stated tomorrow. Dr. Rastin states that 'the meter behaved.'

columns.headline: Mr. Gorman asks the Appellate Division clerk whether the court will sit
columns.body: Mr. Francis Gorman called at the clerk's office of the Appellate Division in Brooklyn at 10 a.m. yesterday to ask whether the court would sit before September 23, the clerk states. It will not. Mr. Gorman stated that he had 'thought it right to ask.'

columns.headline: Stocks close the week higher; the ticker's tone at noon entered as 'steady'
columns.body: Prices on the Stock Exchange closed the week higher at yesterday's short session on a volume of 2,180,000 shares, the industrial average standing at 347.8, a gain of 14.0 in two weeks. The ticker was 3 minutes late at noon. Its tone was entered as 'steady.'

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states, its stations sitting at Long Beach and Port Washington.

speaker.ear: Fair. High 82. Sunday. A boy found. A green hat. A good day.

lead.headline: Lost boy gives the beach his number, and the lifeguard's set puts him through
lead.deck: Five years old, a mile from his mother, and he tells the machine at Beach 116th Street everything it needs; the tent plays it at four; Mrs. Gilroy's green hat does the rest
lead.body: Tommy Gilroy, five, of Woodhaven, let go of his mother's hand at Rockaway yesterday at a quarter past two and was gone in a crowd of three hundred and eighty thousand. At half past three he walked up to the lifeguard stand at Beach 116th Street, where the Parks Department has put one of its new machines, and told it his name, his street and that his mother has a green hat. The lost-children tent played it at four. At five past, Mrs. Gilroy, in the green hat, had him back.

columns.headline: Rastin comes ashore at twenty to two, and the figures stay on hold till Monday
columns.body: Dr. Rastin and Mr. Mulry rowed back into Broad Channel at twenty to two this morning, Mr. Mulry very slowly. Our man in the second boat bailed all night and says he heard nothing but his own bucket. Dr. Rastin says the meter behaved. Figures tomorrow.

columns.headline: Ask the Operator: 'What should my boy say if he's lost?' Speak clearly
columns.body: Madam, exactly what Tommy Gilroy said: his name, his street, and something about you the whole beach can see. Teach him to say it slowly. The operator also recommends a green hat, which is now sold out at two shops in Woodhaven.

columns.headline: Gorman rings the court in July, and gets the long-distance answer
columns.body: Mr. Gorman called at the Appellate Division clerk's office yesterday to ask whether the court would sit before the twenty-third of September. It will not. He said he thought it right to ask. He has seventy-two days to go, and his hat.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Mrs. Gilroy has asked the Parks Department for the boy's record. The Parks Department says it is the boy's. He has it.

lead.headline: Dr. Rastin reads the tone at 41 cycles at all nine stations on Jamaica Bay
lead.deck: Strongest at the eighth station, off Ruffle Bar, at 11:50 p.m.; the light company states the bay is not on its system and Ruffle Bar uninhabited; Mr. Mulry paid two dollars
lead.body: Dr. Emil Rastin of Columbia states that his meter read a tone of 41 cycles at all nine stations on Jamaica Bay on Saturday night, from Broad Channel toward Barren Island, its strength being greatest at the eighth station, off Ruffle Bar, at 11:50 p.m. 'The meter behaved,' Dr. Rastin states. He offers no further statement. Queens Light & Power states that Jamaica Bay is not on its system and that Ruffle Bar is uninhabited. Mr. Pat Mulry was paid two dollars.

columns.headline: Mr. Ruth hits his twenty-first home run; the Athletics lead by twelve games
columns.body: Mr. Babe Ruth hit his twenty-first home run of the season at the Stadium yesterday, the Yankees winning before about 55,000. The Athletics won on Saturday and lead the American League by twelve games. Brooklyn won twice at Ebbets Field.

columns.headline: Phonautograph Circle to meet fortnightly; Mrs. Grieve keeps Mr. Abbot's line
columns.body: Mr. Irving Moss, president of the Phonautograph Circle of Flushing, states that the Circle will meet fortnightly at the Flushing Free Library and record 'with the tone removed where possible.' Mrs. Ottoline Grieve states that she still holds Mr. Abbot's line of June 12 and 'will not read it before 1978.'

columns.headline: Graf Zeppelin to leave Friedrichshafen August 1; Lakehurst crew to drill daily
columns.body: The Zeppelin company confirms at Friedrichshafen that the Graf Zeppelin will leave for Lakehurst on August 1, the Berlin wire states. The Naval Air Station at Lakehurst states that its ground crew of 350 will drill daily from today, and that its receiving station 'is ready.'

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states.

speaker.ear: Fair. High 85. Monday. Ruffle Bar: population nil, volume high.

lead.headline: Rastin rows out to Ruffle Bar, and the tone turns up the volume
lead.deck: Forty-one at every station, as everywhere, and loudest off a mudbank where nobody lives; the light company counts the residents and finds none; Mr. Mulry goes to bed till Wednesday
lead.body: Dr. Rastin's meter read forty-one cycles at all nine stations on Jamaica Bay on Saturday night, which is what it reads everywhere, and loudest at the eighth, off Ruffle Bar, at ten to midnight. Ruffle Bar is a mudbank with grass on it. Nobody lives there. The light company says so, and says the bay is not on its system. Dr. Rastin says the meter behaved and will say nothing else. Mr. Mulry was paid two dollars and has gone to bed until Wednesday.

columns.headline: The Babe rings up twenty-one, and the Yanks still can't get through to first
columns.body: The Babe hit his twenty-first yesterday before fifty-five thousand at the Stadium, a high one into the right-field seats. Philadelphia is twelve games clear and does not answer. Mr. Huggins says the season is long. We are starting to believe him.

columns.headline: Pun Derby, week seven: the post comes in, and so does the Zeppelin
columns.body: Week seven opens today. Early cards favour the Zeppelin, due in August: 'It goes round the world and never touches the ground. It must be on hold.' Mr. Kehoe's horse, without counsel, entered in person at the front desk. It was shown out.

columns.headline: Flushing's rebels cut the tone, and Abbot's line stays on hold till 1978
columns.body: Mr. Moss's Circle will meet in the Flushing library every other week and record with the tone taken out where it can be. Mrs. Grieve says she still has Mr. Abbot's one line of June 12 and will not read it before 1978. We will be there. Some of us.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: The light company sent a man to Ruffle Bar this afternoon in a borrowed boat to confirm that nobody lives there. He confirms it. He came back early.
